changelog: **External Correction — signal averaging (all modes):** new "Use signal average" toggle computes the mouse correction from a sliding-window mean of the sender frames instead of individual frames. Window configurable 1–40 ms (1 ms steps). A second switch chooses whether to average over **all** received frames or **only non-zero** frames — when non-zero mode has no non-zero frame in the window (target momentarily lost), the correction state is held instead of being pulled toward centre. Averaging runs as a pre-stage before the mode logic, so it applies uniformly to Classic / Adaptive / Jump / Snap / Robust.

**Device identification via hardware ID:** the `ping` response now carries `hw_id`, the Teensy's unique chip ID (OCOTP fuse, 8-hex). The web interface and `modifier-control.py` show it in the header and **bind the saved MIM profile slots to it** — with two Teensys, each unit keeps its own profiles (browser `localStorage` / `modifier_settings.json` keyed per device). Existing profiles migrate once to the default / first-device namespace; firmware without `hw_id` falls back to a shared "default" set (no regression).

**External Correction — object gate, switch-frames and prediction removed.** Target selection and prediction now run on the sender side, so the firmware-side object gate, N-consistent-frame object switching and `vel·age` prediction (and the Robust "Switch-Margin" that depended on the gate) were removed from firmware and GUI. The Robust α-β tracker (α / KP / KD, latency compensation) is unchanged.
